items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-05-26
items.q: that had no part of Maryland. Maryland should have been with its own harmony, but they added a tune to themself that Leo Feist made money on it, and they got nothing.

ctx.x: But also, I'd like to ask you, what are some of the tunes Bix recorded that you remember?

Well, he made Tomlin, blues, many of the Dixieland numbers. Then he did like the rest of them did. Took another tune, rehashed the Dixieland number, and he called it his own. Yeah. All musicians began to get the idea. And the closest that I had seen came to it was the Bob Crosby bunch. They take my fidgeted feet and they called it South Rampart Street Parade. Now, I bet you could play both of them together with only exception in the first part and the last part, the march, the break, the march part, the pudding,…
What did they call it? They called it Maryland.
